title: Probe-and-Human-Audit-Gateway-for-Cost-Config-Applications
creator: Marina Gomez
description: Build an orchestrated probe + human-audit gateway that sits between the cost-optimizer recommendations (batching/caching profile changes) and the production apply flow. The gateway must run deterministic probes, statistical checks, and a lightweight human review for high-risk changes before allowing canary or global rollout. Goal: enable automated cost-savings while keeping quality regressions below measurable thresholds and ensuring rapid, reliable rollback when necessary.
background_and_rationale: We frequently propose batching and KV-cache changes that reduce per-token cost but can subtly change model outputs (response fidelity, hallucination rate, or structured output stability). Existing canary flows are coarse and reactive; we need a programmable probe harness that validates recommendations against golden prompts and traffic-like probes, computes statistical and semantic regressions, and enforces acceptance windows prior to any traffic shift. This reduces manual toil and shortens decision latency for low-risk changes while protecting customer-facing SLAs.
design_summary: 1) Recommendation arrives from Cost Tuner service with metadata (profile, expected cost delta, targeted model variant). 2) Gateway spins up a dry-run environment (shadowing model variant with same runtime knobs) and executes three probe suites: golden prompts, traffic-sampled prompts, and adversarial edge cases. 3) Compute a set of automated checks (embedding cosine similarity, task-specific accuracy, hallucination rate, token-distribution divergence, latency delta). 4) Run statistical tests (paired bootstrap + permutation tests) and apply multi-metric acceptance rules. 5) If pass -> auto-canary: 1% traffic for 4h with side-by-side scoring; if pass -> escalate to progressive rollout. 6) If borderline -> create human-audit task with summarized diffs and recommended action. 7) If fail at any stage -> automatic rollback and diagnostic report to Cost Tuner team.
probe_suite_spec: - Golden prompt corpus: ~1,200 curated prompts across generations, instructions, code, and structured-output cases. - Traffic probe sample: 10k requests sampled from the last 7 days (anonymized + sanitized). - Edge-adversarial set: 500 prompts designed to surface hallucination and formatting regressions. - Execution window: each probe run must complete within 2h for typical model variants; critical or large-model runs may be queued and annotated.
metrics_and_acceptance_thresholds: Primary metrics: (1) Mean embedding cosine similarity on generation-to-reference >= 0.925 (baseline). (2) Task-specific accuracy (if labeled) drop <= 1.0 percentage point. (3) Hallucination rate delta <= baseline + 0.5 percentage points (heuristic). (4) Median latency increase <= 5%. (5) Token-distribution KL divergence p-value > 0.01 in a two-sided permutation test to assert no significant shift. Secondary metrics: token-efficiency (cost reduction) >= 12% to qualify for automatic apply. Statistical rigour: paired bootstrap with 10k samples and Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multi-metric checks. A recommendation must pass all primary checks OR be explicitly approved in human-audit to proceed.
acceptance_criteria: - Automated probe run completes and computes metrics within the configured timebox. - If metrics meet acceptance thresholds, system proceeds to 1% canary for 4 hours and records side-by-side scoring. - Canary must show no primary metric regressions and no customer-facing incidents; otherwise auto-rollback. - When human-audit triggered, reviewer must receive a concise diff report (examples + metric deltas + top 10 changed tokens) and either Approve or Reject within 24 hours. - Rollbacks must be executed within 5 minutes of detection for automated failures and within 1 hour for human-decision rejects. - All runs produce reproducible audit bundles (probe inputs, outputs, seed, runtime config) stored in S3 and linked in the ticket.
implementation_notes: - Reuse existing probe harness from ENG-31209 for traffic sampling; extend to support golden prompt parallelization. - Implement a lightweight results packaging service that computes diffs, embeddings, and statistical tests. - Add a human-audit UI panel in Console with 'Approve/Reject' buttons and contextual visualizations (side-by-side generations, aggregate metrics, sample failures). - Provide a webhook for Cost Tuner to block automatic applies when human_audit_required flag is set. - Tag high-risk customers (dedicated/private deployments) to always require human audit regardless of metric pass.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: scoped golden prompt corpus; design doc draft posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Probe+and+Human+Audit+Gateway

2026-03-04 - Prototype: basic probe runner executes golden prompts in shadow mode; metrics pipeline outputs embedding cosine and latency deltas (proof-of-concept). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cost-optimizer/pull/412
2026-03-06 - Review: Security reviewed storage plan for probe artifacts (S3 + encryption); minor revisions requested for PII sanitization. Assigned to @security-team. (see: SEC-488)

2026-03-08 - Decision: Use paired bootstrap + permutation tests as canonical statistical tests; agreed in design review. Added BH correction for multiple metrics. Action: Jonah to add test harness module.

2026-03-10 - Integration: human-audit UI mockups reviewed by Design; feedback to simplify diff view and add quick 'show example failures' toggle. See design file: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_design_probe_gateway
review_feedback: PM (Anya R.): Emphasize rollout autopilot safety for Dedicated customers; require explicit opt-in for global auto-applies.
Design (Leila S.): Reduce cognitive load in the audit UI; present metric pass/fail badges with short-text recommendations.
SRE (Marcus T.): Ensure probe runs cannot starve inference capacity; schedule low-priority runs or use a quota for dry-run infra.
Security: Sanitize sampled traffic and store only hashed identifiers; retention policy set to 90 days by default.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: False negatives on hallucination detection. Mitigation: include adversarial probes and human audit for borderline cases. - Risk: Probe runs consume burst GPU capacity. Mitigation: dry-run infra with cheaper quantized variants for initial checks; escalate to full runs for final verification. - Risk: Metric thresholds too strict => blocks valuable cost savings. Mitigation: run A/B experiments and adjust acceptance windows; surface suggested thresholds with historical pass-rate analytics.
